presentation.summary: Encrypted Matrix notifications for new Silo library content.
presentation.description_markdown: Send new movies and episodes directly from Silo to an encrypted Matrix room, with native poster attachments, episode grouping and persistent delivery state. Administrator access only.
presentation.setup_markdown: Configure the Silo administrator API key, Matrix bot, encrypted room and a writable persistent directory. Open Surimatrix to check the connection and send a poster test. Enable automatic notifications and schedule the New content task every minute.

capabilities.description: Administrator-only delivery of Silo notifications, playback events, watchdog and failure alerts.
Administrator-only Gotify connection and alert settings.

Checks Silo's stream nodes, restart state, database and Redis, and the server's disk and memory, and sends a Gotify alert (and a recovery alert) to admins who turned it on. Needs the read-only Silo key. Suggested schedule: every 5 minutes.

Sends admins who turned it on a Gotify summary of the last 7 days: plays, time watched, top viewers and top titles. Each admin picks their own day and hour (default Sunday 18:00, in their time zone) and a run sends it in that hour or in any later run within 6 hours after (so a week isn't lost if Silo was down), at most once a week, so schedule it to run every hour. Needs the read-only Silo key. Suggested schedule: every 1 hour.

Checks newly added movies and episodes with a resumable catalog cursor. Suggested schedule: every 2 minutes. No initial library flood. Requires admin:monitor:read. Posters/overview depend on host availability.

global_config_schema.title: Surify
global_config_schema.description: Administrator-only Gotify delivery. Shared defaults are optional; each administrator can use a separate destination.

fields.label: Shared Gotify server URL (optional)
fields.description: The shared application token is only used for this exact server URL.

fields.label: Shared Gotify application token (optional)
fields.description: Optional shared token for administrators using the configured shared Gotify server URL.

fields.label: Public URL override (optional)
fields.description: Base URL for "Open in Silo" links. Defaults to the server's configured public URL.

fields.label: Read-only Silo key (admin:monitor:read)
fields.description: Required for automatic delivery. The plugin verifies that recipients are still enabled administrators. Use only the admin:monitor:read scope; configure it from the Surify panel.

fields.label: Stream-control Silo key (optional)
fields.description: Only needed to stop streams. Leave blank when editing to keep the saved secret.

sections.title: Silo API keys (optional)
sections.description: Scoped keys let the plugin read from Silo without full admin access. Silo's API Keys page creates only full-access keys, so the easiest way to get these is to open Admin > Surify as an admin and use "Set up the read-only key": paste a full-access key once and the plugin creates the scoped keys, saves them here and can revoke the full-access key.

presentation.summary: Administrator-only Silo notifications through Gotify: playback, watchdogs, failures and server health.
presentation.description_markdown:
![Surify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/deejayexe/silo-plugin-suricata/main/plugins/surify/web/surify-logo.webp)

Send Silo notifications to a self-hosted Gotify server. Administrator notifications, episode grouping, quiet hours, custom templates, playback and failure alerts, stream watchdogs, server health and recovery checks, weekly digests and links to Silo’s native activity page. Uses the same Silo events and scoped Silo API calls as the MIT-licensed plugin by Josh Black. Gotify uses application tokens, Markdown links and priorities 0, 2, 5, 8 and 10. Sounds and device selection are managed in the Gotify client. New library content can include a Markdown poster and Android big image when Silo exposes a usable image URL. Repeating alerts and binary poster uploads are not supported. Access is restricted to administrators on their primary profile. Other users cannot see the navigation entry or access the pages/API. Before background delivery, Silo must confirm the recipient is still an enabled administrator. Connections from older builds remain inactive until saved by the administrator after upgrading.
presentation.setup_markdown:
1. Sign in to Silo as an administrator on your primary profile. Open Surify from the administrator navigation.
2. Create a Gotify application and copy its private application token (legacy or gtfya.…). Save the server URL and token on the Connection tab. After upgrading from an earlier build, save the existing connection once to activate administrator-only delivery.
3. Check the server and send a test notification.
4. Set up the scoped Silo read-only key (admin:monitor:read). Automatic delivery requires this key to verify recipient roles. Live sessions are available in Silo’s native Admin > Activity page.
5. Configure server alerts. Bind health_check to every 5 minutes and weekly_digest to every hour, then restart Silo after changing task bindings. Ordinary users and secondary profiles cannot access this plugin. 
6. For the new library content alert, enable New library content in Server alerts, bind recently_added to an interval of 2 minutes, and restart Silo after changing the binding. Existing library items are not announced. Artwork uses public/resolved Silo URLs when available.

capabilities.description: Review and manage versions within a Silo library.

global_config_schema.title: Silo connection
global_config_schema.description: Administrator API key with access to the catalog and administrative file queries.

fields.label: Administrator API key
fields.description: Stored by Silo. Leave blank when editing to keep the saved secret.

fields.label: Server URL (optional)
fields.description: Without /api/v2. Set only when an explicit server address is needed.

fields.label: Profile name (optional)
fields.description: Uses the primary profile of the API key account by default. A profile ID is also accepted.

global_config_schema.title: Scan
global_config_schema.description: Up to 100,000 items per query, including episodes; scans stop after 2 hours. Respects Retry-After and stops if Silo continues rejecting requests.

fields.label: Maximum requests per second
fields.description: 1–100 requests/s. Default: 100. Use a dedicated plugin API key configured for 100 requests/s, 6000/min and burst 100. Retry-After is respected.

fields.label: Concurrent requests
fields.description: 1–16 simultaneous requests. Default: 16. The shared plugin request rate still applies.

global_config_schema.title: File deletion
global_config_schema.description: Disabled by default. Requires write access. Empty episode folders are cleaned up within the authorized root; companion files are retained.

fields.label: Authorized folders (one absolute path per line)
fields.description: Real paths inside the Silo container. Library symlinks must resolve inside these folders. The filesystem root / is not allowed.

presentation.summary: Version management for your Silo libraries. Review and remove duplicate items.
presentation.description_markdown: Compare movie and episode versions by path, size, codecs, duration and edition. Optional manual deletion retains another verified path. Hardlinks are supported. No direct database access. Includes resumable in-memory analysis history and responsive mobile version cards. Shows estimated released space per deleted file and per analysis, including history.
presentation.setup_markdown:
1. Save an administrator API key.
2. Open Duplicata Versions, check the connection and scan a library.
3. To delete files, configure authorized real folders, enable deletion and allow write access in the Silo container. Scan again after changing settings.
4. Review the resolved path and retained copy before confirming. Deletion is permanent. Silo updates its catalog on its next library scan.

Results are held in memory. Use at your own risk; you are responsible for accidental deletion and misuse.
